issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a class named Meal (fully implemented with name, ingredients, and getters), but the template repository does not provide Meal (Meal.java is empty) and instead contains an Order class with the same structure. This naming/TYPE mismatch (Meal vs Order) is a structural inconsistency: students will be told a Meal class exists and should be used, but the template lacks it and provides Order, causing confusion and preventing straightforward implementation of SealSaloon and tests that refer to Meal.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template to include a properly implemented Meal class matching the problem statement (name, ingredients, constructor, getters). Remove or rename the Order.java in the template to Meal.java (or ensure both exist and the instructions consistently reference the same class name). Also update the template Main and any comments to use Meal consistently so students can follow the exercise without renaming confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to the core entity as 'Meal' (class Meal with name and ingredients), while the template repository provides an 'Order' class (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Order.java) and an empty Meal.java. This mismatched naming for the same conceptual entity (a meal/order consisting of a name and ingredient list) creates confusion for students mapping requirements to the starter code and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across artifacts. Rename the template's Order class/file to Meal (class Meal in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java) and update any references (e.g., Main) so the template, problem statement, and solution consistently use 'Meal' for the same conceptual entity.
